title: FALA: Locality-Aware PIM-Host Cooperation for Graph Processing with Fine-Grained Column Access
problem: Graph processing exhibits irregular memory access patterns that cause significant memory bandwidth waste on DRAM architectures: cache-based graph tiling suffers from overfetching due to the mismatch between DRAM burst size and the sparse data actually needed, while PIM-based approaches fail to exploit cache locality for high-reuse workloads.
motivation: Graph processing is fundamental to social networks, recommendation systems, and analytics, but neither cache-based nor PIM-only approaches solve the dual challenge of burst overfetching for sparse accesses and cache underutilization for reused data.
method: FALA combines two processing approaches: a CPU with its cache, and processing-in-memory (PIM—computing hardware built into DRAM banks). It uses fine-grained column access to let the system fetch only the specific columns (graph vertices) it actually needs, rather than full DRAM rows, which eliminates bandwidth waste from pulling data you don't actually use. A locality-aware policy routes frequently-used vertex data through the CPU cache, while irregular accesses get processed directly near-memory via PIM. This combined strategy cuts unnecessary memory traffic while fully utilizing both DRAM bandwidth and CPU cache.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a fine-grained column access mechanism within DRAM banks (allowing selective access to individual vertices instead of full rows) combined with a locality-aware policy that routes frequently-accessed vertex data through the host CPU cache and irregular accesses through processing-in-memory.
contributions: Fine-grained column access mechanism within DRAM banks for sparse graph vertex access without full-row overfetching
Locality-aware PIM-host cooperation policy distinguishing high-reuse (cache) from low-reuse (PIM) vertex accesses
1.56x geometric mean speedup and 35.3% energy reduction vs. prior art across cache-based, PIM, and hybrid graph accelerators
Hybrid architecture overcoming limitations of both pure cache-based and pure PIM approaches for graph processing

metrics.speedup: 1.56x geometric mean speedup vs. prior art
